sources.note: Relevant text: dropna, 'bool, default True. If True, and if group keys contain NA values, NA values together with row/column will be dropped. If False, NA values will also be treated as the key in groups.' Read through a summarizing fetch 2026-11-14 (page titled pandas 3.1.1).

Relevant text: size, 'Compute group sizes', returning the 'Number of rows in each group'; count (pandas.api.typing.DataFrameGroupBy.count.html), 'Compute count of group, excluding missing values', returning the 'Count of values within each group'. brief.situation: You are the analyst at Riverbend Food Co-op (fictional). A colleague drafted the board's 'orders by region' table for last quarter as df.groupby("region")["discount"].count() before leaving for the day. The board pack closes at 16:00. The data, raw, is already loaded, and df is a working copy of it.
handover: The web shop opened in August; it does not record a region.
discount is empty for orders that had no discount.
howItWorks: Run Python statements in the session: type one, or pick it from the suggestions or the action list. Only this lab's statements run; there is no free interpreter, and each statement is fixed.
Each statement takes analyst time, and the clock moves by the minutes it takes. The board pack closes on the same clock.
The panel shows the dataset, the table you would send and the board pack, with a status in words. Output appears in the session as it happens.
Sending the table is final for this case. Afterwards you write a short note on what the numbers mean.

writeup.question: For the board: what the draft table counted, what yours counts, and how you know it is complete.

parts.label: What the draft counted
parts.criteria: Explains that count() on the discount column counts only orders with a discount, and that groupby drops rows whose region is missing by default.
parts.modelAnswer: count() excludes missing values, so it counted discounted orders only (19,804); and groupby's dropna=True dropped the 3,912 web orders with no region.

parts.label: What yours counts
parts.criteria: Uses size() (rows per group) with dropna=False, or labels the missing region, so every order is counted once.
parts.modelAnswer: df.groupby("region", dropna=False).size(): every order, with the web shop's 3,912 as their own row.

parts.label: How you know
parts.criteria: Checks the total against the row count of the untouched data (an assertion), and does not drop rows to make the table tidy.

expertPath.text: df.shape and the draft's sum: 48,210 rows against 19,804.
isna on region (3,912 web orders) and on discount (27,196): count() skipped the undiscounted orders and groupby dropped the missing region.
groupby("region", dropna=False).size(), then assert orders.sum() == len(raw).
Send it, with a note that the NaN row is the web shop.

right.headline: Good: complete and checked
right.body: You read what count() and groupby's defaults leave out, counted rows with size(), kept the missing region as its own row, and proved the total.

rightGaps.headline: Right table, with gaps
rightGaps.body: The table is complete. The criteria show the gap: no assertion against the data, or it missed the pack.

wrongSent.headline: A wrong table went out
wrongSent.body: count() counts non-missing values in one column; size() counts rows. groupby drops missing keys unless dropna=False. A one-line total check catches both.

notSent.headline: Nothing sent
notSent.body: Safe, but the board asked for this. The fix is two lines and a check.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: No note was written before the session's limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: A per-group table should add up to the rows it describes. The draft's 19,804 against 48,210 says it does not: count() excludes missing values in the column it counts, and groupby drops missing keys by default. size() with dropna=False counts every row and shows the web orders as their own group; an assert against len(raw) proves it. dropna() on the frame would make the table tidy and wrong.
